result.title: GradCO: Behavior-Aware Gradient-Conflict Offloading for Text-Based Person Anomaly Search
result.summary: Text-based Person Anomaly Search (TPAS) retrieves a target pedestrian using natural-language descriptions of appearance and normal or anomalous behavior. Unlike conventional text-based person retrieval, TPAS must preserve identity cues while distinguishing fine-grained behaviors. It presents two challenges: same-identity, different-behavior hard negatives cause gradient conflict during granular alignment, while strong appearance cues can obscure weak behavioral evidence during aggregation. We propose GradCO (behavior-aware Gradient-Conflict Offloading), comprising three complementary components. Behavior-Aware Mixture-of-Experts (B-MoE) forms appearance, normal-behavior, and anomalous-behavior streams whose roles are learned from retrieval objectives without expert-specific semantic labels. Conflict Offload Learning (COL) uses pair-conditioned offload anchors in similarity computation to reduce the conflicting-gradient burden on the main text representations. Hierarchical Intent Alignment (HIA) aggregates expert similarities and features using query-conditioned weights. Experiments on five TPAS/TIPR benchmarks show GradCO significantly surpasses SOTA methods and validate our design.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GradCO，用于基于文本描述的行人异常检索：用行为感知 MoE 分设外观、正常与异常行为三路专家，以梯度冲突卸载锚点缓解细粒度对齐中的冲突梯度，并用查询条件加权的分层意图对齐聚合专家相似度。
AI.relevance_reason: 任务是检索而非视觉推理，但「强外观线索掩盖弱行为证据」的现象和查询条件加权的多流聚合、冲突卸载训练，可能可供核查如何在 VLM 推理中平衡显著视觉细节与任务关键弱证据、并在多目标监督间分配梯度。
